LESSON: INTEGERS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 1.1: Integers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Integers, part of NUMBERS in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do we apply integers in daily activities?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign vocabularies related to integers,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Integers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform operations on, integers in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Integers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. work out combined operations on integers in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Integers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. apply operations on integers to real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Integers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. promote use of integers in real life situations. ● In groups, learners are guided to fingerspell and sign the basic operations on integers from a given combined operation problem and sign the basic operations of integers in a combined operation problem. ● In pairs, learners are guided to work out the basic operations on integers using number cards and charts. ● In groups, learners are guided to play games involving numbers and their operations. ● In pairs, learners are guided to carry out combined operations of integers in the correct order. How do we apply integers in daily activities? 2 ● In purposive groups, learners are guided to carry out activities involving positive and negative integers such as reading temperature changes on a thermometer and discussing how to record it. ● In groups, learners are guided to record temperatures above zero degrees Celsius as positive integers. Where possible, record temperatures below zero in degrees Celsius as negative integers. ● In groups, learners are guided to use digital devices or other resources such as print to carry out operations on integers. ● In pairs, learners are guided to play creative games involving integers. 3

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Integers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: Uses creativity in work context as the learner works out combined operations

of integers in the correct order.

● Learning to learn: Knows what doing well looks like as the learner carries out activities such as reading temperature

changes in a thermometer and discussing how to record it.

● Digital literacy: operates digital devices: as the learners use digital devices to determine temperature.

Values:
● Respect: As learners work in groups to carry out activities such as reading temperature changes in a thermometer and

discuss how to record it.

● Unity: As learners work together in groups towards achieving set goals of reading thermometers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Life skills and value education: As learners read and record their body temperatures.

Link to other learning areas:

● The learner is able to relate the skill of reading temperature to the concept of weather changes in Social Studies.

Suggested learning resources:

● Number lines, games on charts, number cards, steps, up and down stairs, digital devices
